Compares your walk to the car with your own normal walk
Sensing is stopped. Tap Start to turn it on.
Turn on the check to start learning your normal walk. Nothing is recorded while it is off.

PervasiveSense will learn how you normally walk from your everyday walking (best after 1–2 weeks), then compare the walk to your car with it.

• It flags walking that is unusual for you, not alcohol itself. Tiredness, an injury, new shoes or a heavy bag can also change your walk.
• It only gives advice. It is not a breathalyser and never legal evidence.
• Everything stays on this phone. You can turn it off or forget the learned data at any time.

How it works and its limits

• Learns only your own walking: no drinking data is needed.
• Compares side-to-side sway, step timing, stride regularity and turning with your normal walk; a check is unusual only if most of the walk is.
• Flags unusual impairment, not alcohol itself, and only advises.
• Never legal evidence. All processing stays on this phone.
• Basis: in a lab study, phone sensors detected breath alcohol above 0.08% from walking with 92.5% accuracy; side-to-side sway was the strongest signal.

Alert my contact if I drive after a warning

Within an hour of a warning, if your car’s Bluetooth connects or the driving looks unsteady (also after a slightly unusual walk), your contact gets a text message (with your location, if allowed) and, if you allow it, a call. You always get 30 seconds to cancel, for example as a passenger.\nEvery other drive is watched too, even if you never checked your walk: if the driving looks clearly unsteady, the phone asks “Are you OK?”. No answer within 60 seconds alerts your contact.\nA fall (fall detection) asks “Are you OK?” the same way.
